Polar Posts Steady Trade Volumes Amid Stable Market Conditions

Polar, a leading player in Russia’s Metals & Mining sector, reported routine trade figures for the second quarter of 2024, signaling continued operational stability amid broadly unchanged market conditions. The company exported 1.12 million metric tons of refined metals between April and June, in line with the 1.09 million tons shipped during the first quarter.

According to a company statement released Thursday, demand for Polar’s core products—primarily nickel and copper—remained robust across European and Asian markets. “We are maintaining consistent export levels, supported by stable production and reliable logistics,” said Leonid Vlasov, Polar’s Chief Commercial Officer. “No significant changes in supply or demand have been observed this quarter.”

Industry analysts noted the absence of any notable disruptions in the wider sector. “The metals market has been remarkably steady so far this year,” commented Darya Mirova of the Eurasian Commodities Association. “Polar’s trade data reflects a broader trend of normalization after recent years of volatility.”

Domestic deliveries also followed expected patterns, with Polar supplying approximately 240,000 metric tons to Russian manufacturers, a figure unchanged from the previous quarter. Production at Polar’s main facilities in Norilsk and Kandalaksha continued uninterrupted, according to union representatives.

Export revenues for the quarter are expected to align closely with last year’s results, given the stable average price for nickel and copper on global exchanges. Polar’s management reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining current output levels for the remainder of 2024, citing strong order books and ongoing international demand.
